comparisons.peer_summary: Long-term supplier relationships enable the proactive management of technology development and product discontinuance plans, as well as the monitoring of suppliers' financial health.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom disclose supplier relationship management strategies within Item 1, though they focus on different aspects of supply chain sustainability. NVIDIA specifically targets the engagement of manufacturing suppliers to adopt science-based emissions targets, as stated: 'By fiscal year 2026, we aim to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of NVIDIA's scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions with goal of effecting supplier adoption of science-based targets.' Broadcom focuses on using long-term supplier relationships for proactive technology and financial health management rather than explicit emissions targets: 'Our long-term relationships with our suppliers allow us to proactively manage our technology development and product discontinuance plans, and to monitor our suppliers' financial health.' While both address supplier engagement in the context of risk and strategy, NVIDIA's disclosure is quantified around Scope 3 GHG reduction, whereas Broadcom's is qualitative regarding operational and financial stability.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company sets company-wide environmental goals to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, energy, water use, and waste, linking a portion of executive and employee performance bonuses in 2024 to reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 25,000 metric tons compared to 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both disclose environmental goals related to greenhouse gas emissions, but they differ in their approach to accountability and scope. NVIDIA explicitly aims to drive supplier adoption of science-based targets for Scope 3 emissions through engagement, stating: 'By fiscal year 2026, we aim to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of NVIDIA's scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions with goal of effecting supplier adoption of science-based targets.' Intel links executive and employee compensation directly to achieving specific Scope 1 and 2 emission reduction targets, stating: 'In 2024, we linked a portion of the executive and employee performance bonus to our goal to reduce our 2024 Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, compared to 2023.' While both companies set emissions reduction goals, NVIDIA focuses on third-party Scope 3 supplier alignment, whereas Intel uses internal financial incentives for direct Scope 1 and 2 reductions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm has established science-based emissions reduction targets approved by the SBTi, including a 50% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2030, a 25% reduction in absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 2030, and reaching net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA disclose science-based emissions reduction targets aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), indicating a shared strategic approach to climate change mitigation. Qualcomm outlines its specific numerical goals: 'Qualcomm has established near- and long-term science-based emissions reduction targets, which have been approved by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), including: (1) reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; (2) reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 from a 2020 base year; and (3) reach net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by 2040.' Similarly, NVIDIA states its goal to effect supplier adoption of science-based targets: 'By fiscal year 2026, we aim to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of NVIDIA's scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions with goal of effecting supplier adoption of science-based targets.' Both companies utilize the SBTi framework and address Scope 3 emissions, though Qualcomm provides explicit percentage reduction milestones while NVIDIA describes a process goal for supplier engagement.
